To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
screening effects of the nuclear medium on the interaction between two static charges may lead to oscillations in the potential.
the potential in dense plasmas can exhibit a non-monotonic oscillating behaviour due to poles in the boson propagators, which is not present in the Debye screened QED potential.
The one-pion exchange potential between two static nucleons in a nuclear medium can exhibit a Yukawa oscillatory behavior.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of screening effects in relativistic models of dense matter at finite temperature.
the study of screening effects in relativistic models of dense matter at finite temperature.
the study of the analytic properties of the one-bosons exchange propagators in dense matter, in order to investigate the screening effects in relativistic models of dense matter.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the existence of Yukawa oscillations depends on the model and on the density/temperature.
the Yukawa oscillations are a generic feature of the one-bosonic exchange in the one-bose-exchange approximation.
the Yukawa oscillations appear in the one-pion and one-gluon exchange models of nuclear matter and quark-gluone plasma, respectively, at low densities and/or temperatures.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Yukawa oscillation is not a universal phenomenon.
, at high densities, Yukawa oscillations are more important than Friedel oscillations in the nuclear medium.
the Yukawa oscillations in the potential interaction are related to the presence of a pole on the corresponding propagator.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the screening potential is not a simple function of the distance between the 'charges'.
the screening effects in dense matter are richer than previously thought, since they can lead to oscillatory potentials.
the potential interaction can exhibit an oscillating behavior, which is not due to the medium, but to the analytic structure in the $q-$plane of the boson propagators.
